## Observed Currents

Read current speed and direction from NOAA current-meter stations. Requires station_id, start_date and end_date (inclusive UTC dates, YYYY-MM-DD). Returns speed_mps with typed UTC timestamps, station_id, source_url and fetched_at. Speeds are m/s converted from NOAA cm/s. Current predictions describe flow, and slack must not be inferred from high or low tide.  Requests are split into non-overlapping chunks of at most seven days; all-bin observations use one-day chunks. Missing measurements become NULL and observation flags remain unmodified. Explicit NOAA no-data responses produce no rows; other API errors fail. NULL arguments are rejected. No API key required.

### Result columns

| Column | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| station_id | NOAA station identifier; retain as text, including leading zeroes. |
| time | UTC timestamp of the current observation. |
| speed_mps | Observed current speed in m/s, converted from NOAA cm/s. |
| direction_deg | Direction toward which the current flows, degrees from true north. |
| bin | Observed depth-bin identifier; use current_bins for deployed sensor depths. |
| flags | Unmodified NOAA quality flags, when available. |
| source_url | Exact NOAA request URL; identifies the data product and request parameters. |
| fetched_at | UTC time the NOAA response was retrieved; not the observation time. |
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Inspect observed currents in UTC","sql":"SELECT time, speed_mps FROM tides.main.currents('cb0102', '2026-01-01', '2026-01-02') ORDER BY time"},{"description":"Mean and peak observed current speed by sensor depth at Cape Henry (cb0102) on 1 January 2026, joining all-bin observations to the current-meter bin depths","sql":"SELECT b.bin, b.depth_m, round(avg(c.speed_mps), 3) AS mean_speed_mps, round(max(c.speed_mps), 3) AS max_speed_mps FROM tides.main.currents('cb0102', '2026-01-01', '2026-01-01') AS c JOIN tides.main.current_bins('cb0102') AS b USING (bin) GROUP BY b.bin, b.depth_m ORDER BY b.bin"}]

## Tidal Current Predictions

Read predicted slack, flood and ebb events or interval major-axis currents. Requires station_id, start_date and end_date (inclusive UTC dates, YYYY-MM-DD). Returns velocity_major_mps with typed UTC timestamps, station_id, source_url and fetched_at. Speeds are m/s converted from NOAA cm/s. Current predictions describe flow, and slack must not be inferred from high or low tide. velocity_major_mps is signed along the major axis; mean flood/ebb directions are not instantaneous bearings. Default step=max_slack; bin=1.  Requests are split into non-overlapping chunks of at most seven days; all-bin observations use one-day chunks. Missing measurements become NULL and observation flags remain unmodified. Explicit NOAA no-data responses produce no rows; other API errors fail. NULL arguments are rejected. No API key required.

### Result columns

| Column | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| station_id | NOAA station identifier; retain as text, including leading zeroes. |
| time | UTC timestamp of the current prediction. |
| velocity_major_mps | Signed velocity along the major axis in m/s: positive flood, negative ebb; NOAA cm/s divided by 100. |
| event_type | NOAA event type, typically flood, ebb, or slack for max_slack; NULL for interval samples. |
| flood_direction_deg | Mean flood direction in degrees from true north; not an instantaneous bearing. |
| ebb_direction_deg | Mean ebb direction in degrees from true north; not an instantaneous bearing. |
| bin | Depth-bin identifier supplied by NOAA. |
| depth_m | NOAA prediction-bin depth in metres. |
| source_url | Exact NOAA request URL; identifies the data product and request parameters. |
| fetched_at | UTC time the NOAA response was retrieved; not the observation time. |
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Inspect tidal current predictions in UTC","sql":"SELECT time, velocity_major_mps FROM tides.main.current_predictions('ACT0956', '2026-01-01', '2026-01-02') ORDER BY time"},{"description":"Check each predicted slack, maximum flood and maximum ebb at the Chesapeake Bay entrance (cb0102, bin 4) on 1 January 2026 against the mean observed speed within 15 minutes of the event","sql":"SELECT p.time, p.event_type, round(abs(p.velocity_major_mps), 2) AS predicted_speed_mps, round(avg(o.speed_mps), 2) AS observed_speed_mps, count(o.speed_mps) AS observations FROM tides.main.current_predictions('cb0102', '2026-01-01', '2026-01-01', bin := 4) AS p JOIN tides.main.currents('cb0102', '2026-01-01', '2026-01-01', bin := 4) AS o ON o.time BETWEEN p.time - INTERVAL 15 MINUTE AND p.time + INTERVAL 15 MINUTE GROUP BY p.time, p.event_type, p.velocity_major_mps ORDER BY p.time"}]

## NOAA Tide and Current Stations

List stations for one NOAA CO-OPS product family. Use station_id with the corresponding tide or current function. The named station_kind defaults to tidepredictions; use waterlevels for observations and currentpredictions/currents for current stations. Returns station names, coordinates, state and NOAA station type; currentpredictions returns one row per prediction depth bin, with bin set (pass it to current_predictions). Filter in SQL; a tide station does not necessarily provide current predictions. No API key is needed. Missing metadata is NULL; NULL arguments are rejected. Data is fetched at query execution and includes source_url and fetched_at.

### Result columns

| Column | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| station_id | NOAA station identifier; retain as text, including leading zeroes. |
| name | Station name supplied by NOAA. |
| latitude | Latitude in decimal degrees, north positive. |
| longitude | Longitude in decimal degrees, east positive. |
| state | US state or territory abbreviation when supplied. |
| station_kind | Requested collection: waterlevels, tidepredictions, currents, or currentpredictions. |
| station_type | NOAA station type code, when supplied; subordinate stations have restricted prediction intervals. |
| bin | Current-prediction depth bin (pass as current_predictions bin); currentpredictions lists one row per bin. NULL for other collections. |
| source_url | Exact NOAA request URL; identifies the data product and request parameters. |
| fetched_at | UTC time the NOAA response was retrieved; not the observation time. |

## Tide Predictions

Read predicted high/low tides or interval water levels from NOAA. Requires station_id, start_date and end_date (inclusive UTC dates, YYYY-MM-DD). Returns height_m with typed UTC timestamps, station_id, source_url and fetched_at. Heights are metres relative to the named datum (default MLLW). Predictions are astronomical, not weather-adjusted water levels.  Requests are split into non-overlapping chunks of at most seven days; all-bin observations use one-day chunks. Missing measurements become NULL and observation flags remain unmodified. Explicit NOAA no-data responses produce no rows; other API errors fail. NULL arguments are rejected. No API key required.

### Result columns

| Column | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| station_id | NOAA station identifier; retain as text, including leading zeroes. |
| time | UTC timestamp of the predicted tide or observed water level. |
| height_m | Water level in metres relative to the datum column; NULL for a missing value. |
| datum | Requested vertical reference, such as MLLW; compare heights only on compatible datums. |
| event_type | H for high tide, L for low tide; NULL for interval samples or observations. |
| sigma_m | Standard deviation in metres for observed water levels; NULL for predictions. |
| quality | NOAA observation quality code: p preliminary or v verified; NULL for predictions. |
| flags | Unmodified NOAA comma-separated observation quality flags; NULL when absent. |
| source_url | Exact NOAA request URL; identifies the data product and request parameters. |
| fetched_at | UTC time the NOAA response was retrieved; not the observation time. |
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Inspect tide predictions in UTC","sql":"SELECT time, height_m FROM tides.main.tide_predictions('8518750', '2026-01-01', '2026-01-02') ORDER BY time"},{"description":"Compare each predicted high tide at The Battery on 1–3 January 2026 with the highest observed water level within an hour of it; surge_m is observed peak minus predicted height","sql":"SELECT p.time AS predicted_high, p.height_m AS predicted_m, max(o.height_m) AS observed_peak_m, round(max(o.height_m) - p.height_m, 3) AS surge_m FROM tides.main.tide_predictions('8518750', '2026-01-01', '2026-01-03') AS p JOIN tides.main.water_levels('8518750', '2026-01-01', '2026-01-03') AS o ON o.time BETWEEN p.time - INTERVAL 1 HOUR AND p.time + INTERVAL 1 HOUR WHERE p.event_type = 'H' GROUP BY p.time, p.height_m ORDER BY p.time"}]
